status: New authorial baseline; indicative estimates, not surveys

profiles.daily_life: Lowland farm households have dependable local produce in ordinary seasons, but rents and levies restrict purchases. Railway and engineering workers have better cash access; court and landed households live far above the mean.
profiles.politics: Provincial estates mediate protection and taxation. Bargaining preserves local liberties unevenly and does not give poorer households equal access to influence.
profiles.review: Freight reliability, estate levies and access to industrial wages.

profiles.daily_life: Food-producing districts can provision themselves while many agricultural households have little disposable income. Industrial wards offer wages under close supervision; landholding families capture much of the surplus.
profiles.politics: Landed recruitment and administrative discipline give order at the expense of ordinary residents' freedom to refuse obligations.
profiles.review: Harvest access, recruitment burdens and distribution of seed and transport improvements.

profiles.daily_life: Commercial towns offer varied food, manufactured goods and skilled employment. Rent and import prices press on dock labourers while finance and precision trades support conspicuous wealth.
profiles.politics: Commercial representation and functioning contracts coexist with concentrated credit and unequal political access.
profiles.review: Imported necessities, urban rents, labour disputes and colonial liabilities.

profiles.daily_life: Cultivated districts and basin trades provide moderate security where water arrives reliably. Households below disputed gates face sharper uncertainty than prosperous engineering towns.
profiles.politics: Water authorities and local assemblies offer remedies, but estate vetoes can delay repairs and shift burdens downstream.
profiles.review: Water reliability and whether the maintenance compact reaches excluded estates.

profiles.daily_life: Agricultural families have modest consumption and lose labour to mobilisation. Skilled town households fare better, but credit dependency limits room for public improvements.
profiles.politics: Military prestige and landed privilege weigh heavily on ordinary households. Shorter reserve rotations ease a real burden without removing it.
profiles.review: Harvest labour, foreign credit and renewed mobilisation demands.

profiles.daily_life: Industry supports substantial skilled wages and urban services, while imported food and fuel make household bills vulnerable. The damaged relay district remains less secure than recovered urban centres.
profiles.politics: Municipal representation gives residents channels to contest policy; industrial labour disputes and uneven recovery still matter.
profiles.review: Import prices, labour conditions and distribution of Hunter-strike recovery.

profiles.daily_life: Interrupted freight, coal fighting and rival tolls make food, heating and regular work unreliable. Secure enclaves and well-connected households retain comforts inaccessible to many residents.
profiles.politics: People depend on competing courts and city authorities. Grain agreements help particular routes but do not provide consistent protection across the region.
profiles.review: Whether the reopened grain corridor holds, local fighting and arbitrary tolls.

profiles.daily_life: Winter stores and valley agriculture support a restrained material life; distant districts have fewer goods and services. Administrative and trading households enjoy much better supply.
profiles.politics: Crown protection is valued where it reaches, but distance and unequal access to officials limit practical remedies.
profiles.review: Winter provisioning, spare parts and the reach of repair programmes.

profiles.daily_life: Skilled mining and industrial work can pay well; ordinary workers remain exposed to hard conditions and imported grain prices. Proprietors benefit disproportionately from mineral sales.
profiles.politics: Mining councils and industrial owners offer uneven representation. Disputed concessions and dependence on employer-linked commerce sustain grievances.
profiles.review: Grain costs, workplace protection and concession disputes.

profiles.daily_life: Material consumption is moderate, with shelter and medical institutions improving security beyond what cash output alone suggests. Remote settlements still have less access than defended towns.
profiles.politics: Wardens, orders and estates exercise substantial authority, but established shelter and care obligations give residents meaningful expectations.
profiles.review: Hospice reach, winter stores and whether service obligations are honoured.

profiles.daily_life: Grain-producing households and river towns benefit from food access and trade. Labourers have fewer comforts than commercial families, but storage improvements reduce some seasonal vulnerability.
profiles.politics: Commercial and agricultural authorities bargain over water and transport; residents' influence varies with property and locality.
profiles.review: Grain prices, water control and the spread of drying improvements.

profiles.daily_life: Ports offer skilled work, imported goods and commercial opportunity; inland households face slower access and fewer services. Shipping wealth is far from evenly distributed.
profiles.politics: Port families and industrial firms dominate national choices, while agricultural districts contest their share of costs.
profiles.review: Food and fuel imports, naval taxation and inland transport access.

profiles.daily_life: Farm and industrial households bear substantial military demands. Procurement supports some jobs, but frontier uncertainty competes with ordinary household priorities.
profiles.politics: Crown and supplier interests carry more weight than poorer residents. De-escalation reduces immediate alarm without ending the burden.
profiles.review: Frontier rotation costs, taxation and whether liaison prevents renewed escalation.

profiles.daily_life: Provincial stores buffer cold districts, though mountain households have limited choice and slow supply. Town trades and larger owners have more secure consumption.
profiles.politics: Provincial bargaining restrains some central demands but makes protection uneven between districts.
profiles.review: Winter stores, reserve rotations and relations with Vardol.

profiles.daily_life: Mountain households combine modest goods access with technical and communal institutions. Trade and water arrangements matter strongly to work and provisioning.
profiles.politics: Republican institutions retain local legitimacy; inherited debts and disputes constrain what they can deliver.
profiles.review: Water releases, repair work and the distribution of debt costs.

profiles.daily_life: Delta cultivation and engineering provide moderate material security, with richer commercial ports beside less prosperous agricultural districts. Water and freight failures quickly reach household budgets.
profiles.politics: Commercial and water authorities supply useful services but also command powerful bargaining positions over inland customers and workers.
profiles.review: Delivery reliability, customs burdens and access to basin repairs.

profiles.daily_life: Plantation output does not translate into comfortable lives for most workers. Grain and livestock districts offer different livelihoods; technical and estate households command far greater purchasing power.
profiles.politics: Estate labour obligations and unequal commercial access are central grievances. Delivery arbitration has not settled labour conditions.
profiles.review: Coercive obligations, land access and whether machinery gains reach workers.

profiles.daily_life: Most households rely on local agricultural and forest markets with limited purchased comforts. Patronage and fragmented tolls affect access to tools and work.
profiles.politics: House courts provide differing protections; there is no equally accessible common remedy or unified authority.
profiles.review: House disputes, freight participation and imported repair costs.

profiles.daily_life: Tenant households face debt and restricted access to cleared land while harbour and plantation owners profit from exports. Predictable seasonal tolls offer some relief to trade.
profiles.politics: Separate land courts and toll assemblies favour different patrons. Tenants' leverage remains weaker than creditors'.
profiles.review: Land debt, toll enforcement and expiry of harvest-season agreements.

profiles.daily_life: Ordinary households have modest farm and wool incomes with costly winter transport. Charter towns and well-financed shipping houses are appreciably better supplied.
profiles.politics: Town privileges protect some merchants; residents outside those charters depend more on estate courts and changing rights of passage.
profiles.review: Fodder, toll changes and access to witnessed trading weights.

profiles.daily_life: Grain, milling and fertiliser work support households when releases arrive on time. A withheld gate can threaten livelihoods far beyond the immediate dispute.
profiles.politics: Separate water commands and councils offer negotiated protection, unevenly enforced across estate boundaries.
profiles.review: Gate maintenance, water allocation and enforceability of arbitration.

profiles.daily_life: Harbour trade supports relatively comfortable skilled households, while indebted rural producers face foreclosure and expensive necessities. Safer convoy departures help without securing every feeder route.
profiles.politics: Commercial conventions protect cargo better than they resolve unequal rural credit or rival seizure claims.
profiles.review: Freight security, harvest debt and disputed cargo seizures.

profiles.daily_life: Concession workers depend on imported food and employer-linked transport; interruption threatens wages and supplies together. Owners retain a much richer standard despite local losses.
profiles.politics: Armed intimidation, lease disputes and contested bonds make redress unreliable. The escrow settlement covers participating claims only.
profiles.review: Strike aftermath, Hunter damage, charter enforcement and grain access.

profiles.daily_life: Winter survival rests on stores, convoy access and reciprocal shelter. Ordinary households have few luxuries; invited hospices improve care in some districts.
profiles.politics: Wardens owe protection, but scarcity tests those obligations and can turn requisition into lasting exaction.
profiles.review: Store access, hospice provision and temporary levies becoming permanent.

profiles.daily_life: Fishing and timber households rely on imported grain and seasonal work. Port merchants and large estates enjoy much greater security than shore crews.
profiles.politics: Customary fishing rights remain vulnerable to estate claims; seasonal settlements offer limited protection.
profiles.review: Grain freight, shore access and succession disputes.

profiles.daily_life: Cultivated valleys and textile or wagon work sustain modest consumption. Repeated tolls reduce ordinary purchasing power while patron-backed towns fare better.
profiles.politics: Protections change between lordships, town liberties and clients. Shared manifests ease inspections but leave separate power structures intact.
profiles.review: Tolls, foreign subsidies and the cost of secure passage.

profiles.daily_life: Granaries and market farming support basic security, though requisitions can remove household reserves. Commercial and landed families remain more comfortable.
profiles.politics: Elected boards, governors and estate courts compete. Written requisition limits improve recourse only where accepted and enforced.
profiles.review: Harvest adequacy, requisition receipts and competing transport demands.

profiles.daily_life: Coastal trade and agriculture provide moderate livelihoods. Seasonal crews and inland villages have less predictable access than chartered port households.
profiles.politics: Communes and houses keep separate rights; pilot and merchant influence exceeds that of casual workers.
profiles.review: Seasonal employment, inland roads and harbour fees.

profiles.daily_life: Skilled engineering and mining support better town consumption than many agricultural neighbours. Imported food and costly coastal transfers erode the benefit for ordinary households.
profiles.politics: Autonomous councils offer local voice and defended approaches, with unequal influence among districts and occupations.
profiles.review: Mine safety, food imports and freight charges; the proposed railway is not yet a benefit.

profiles.daily_life: Productive valleys and arsenals sustain employment, but military commitments and elite consumption absorb much of the surplus. Frontier households bear particularly heavy disruption.
profiles.politics: Central ducal supervision supplies order with limited popular leverage. Rival estate and arsenal interests do not imply an already collapsing state.
profiles.review: Border levies, fuel imports, harvest disruption and military requisitions.

profiles.daily_life: Auvrienne and Serravonne offer skilled work and improving water or railway services; poorer tenants and labourers still have little spare income. Well-connected houses enjoy far greater comfort.
profiles.politics: Chartered institutions permit bargaining and advancement through education or patronage. Poor households bear disproportionate dangerous service; influence shapes access to justice.
profiles.review: Conscription fairness, wages versus food and rent, and whether civil improvements reach poorer districts. The small rifle trial has no assumed national welfare effect.

profiles.daily_life: Ports offer varied goods and skilled maintenance work, but household costs depend on imported food and fuel. Banking and shipping families live much better than casual workers.
profiles.politics: Restricted franchise privileges commercial families. Reliable contracts and escorts do not amount to equal political influence.
profiles.review: Import costs, urban rents, patronage and exclusion from representation.

profiles.daily_life: Fishing, pilotage and repair work sustain island households; grain and fuel prices depend on shipping. Naval and merchant households have more secure stores than outer communities.
profiles.politics: Protection of shipping gives the Admiralty standing, while hereditary and naval offices limit ordinary influence.
profiles.review: Grain reliability, convoy coverage and unequal access among islands.

profiles.daily_life: Terrace farming, fisheries and shared water rights provide useful security despite dependence on imported engines and medicine. Material choice is narrower than in rich mainland ports.
profiles.politics: Island assemblies protect land and elect harbour officers. Customs exemptions and defence levies remain contested between carriers and cultivators.
profiles.review: Import access and whether depot concessions shift costs onto farmers.

profiles.daily_life: Export wealth sits beside much poorer island households. Shipping and credit controlled by outside firms constrain the benefits of local production.
profiles.politics: Village councils retain some land authority, but colonial courts favour stronger commercial access. The levy suspension is a limited concession, not equal treatment.
profiles.review: Compulsory levies, common pasture and the mixed inquiry's actual remedies.

profiles.daily_life: Terrace grain and fisheries support modest household security with imported plant and fuel limiting choice. Technical schooling creates a small route to skilled work.
profiles.politics: Crown decisions require bargains with houses, towns and communal-land custodians; outer communities retain protections against unilateral requisition.
profiles.review: School access, budget reform and preservation of island consent.

profiles.daily_life: Farming and preserved-food exports support basic livelihoods, but winter isolation limits goods and repairs. Settler and crown-linked households often enjoy better access.
profiles.politics: Unequal land and tax arrangements remain despite wider consultation over provisioning.
profiles.review: Winter deliveries, disputed leases and distribution of customs income.

profiles.daily_life: Cash incomes and imported comforts are low, but reciprocal shelter, local food and rescue duties buffer hardship. Severe winters still restrict diet and medical access.
profiles.politics: Hearth assemblies preserve strong local voice and customary land protection without requiring a wealthy central state.
profiles.review: Winter stores, fuel scarcity and whether rescue obligations can be met.

profiles.daily_life: Repair trades, cooperative farming and exports support moderate comfort. Seasonal crews and outer communities have more precarious access than settled port households.
profiles.politics: An elected assembly offers accountability but its residence and tax franchise excludes some residents.
profiles.review: Freight charges, outer representation and foreign-loan burdens.

profiles.daily_life: Cultivation, fishing and communal land provide basic security with limited imported comforts and medical access. Harbour households can purchase more than inland producers.
profiles.politics: Kin councils and elected harbour assemblies protect common land, though local hierarchy and creditor pressure still affect choices.
profiles.review: Medical supplies, harvest debt and keeping communal land outside collateral.

profiles.daily_life: Agriculture, textiles and repairs support moderate consumption, with schooling offering skilled prospects. Machinery and fuel imports constrain opportunities outside the ports.
profiles.politics: Assembly scrutiny restrains borrowing, but landholding and court merchants retain stronger influence than ordinary workers.
profiles.review: Exclusive contracts, school access and the cost of royal borrowing.

profiles.daily_life: Fishing and timber communities depend on winter grain shipments and seasonal work. Settler towns and connected traders generally have better supply than remote communities.
profiles.politics: Treaty councils provide some leverage, but unequal land rights and new concessions remain contentious.
profiles.review: Grain schedules, concession disputes and equal access to harbour services.

profiles.daily_life: Fishing, herding and mutual refuge keep households viable with few manufactured comforts. Short seasons and scarce medicine impose real limits despite strong community support.
profiles.politics: Seasonal moots preserve local control and refuge obligations. Low unrest reflects these relationships, not abundant wealth.
profiles.review: Shipping windows, imported grain and the capacity to honour refuge obligations.
